input: Learn to read music notation from scratch

gold.taskTitle: Learn to read music notation from scratch
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to build the ability to read and understand standard music notation, starting with no prior knowledge.

questions.title: What instrument will you be reading music for?
questions.description: Identifying the instrument shapes which clef, range, and notation style to focus on.

questions.title: What is your current level of musical experience?
questions.description: Understanding whether the user has any background in music theory, playing by ear, or prior notation exposure.

questions.title: What is your target deadline or desired timeframe?
questions.description: Knowing how urgently the user wants to reach reading proficiency helps structure the pace of the plan.

questions.title: How many minutes per day can you practice?
questions.description: Daily time availability determines how intensive or spread-out each learning session should be.

questions.title: Do you prefer self-study, apps, videos, or a teacher?
questions.description: Learning format preference guides which resources and methods to recommend.

questions.title: Is there a specific piece or genre you want to read?
questions.description: A concrete musical goal — such as classical, pop, or a particular song — gives direction and motivation to the plan.

questions.title: Do you need to read rhythm notation or just pitch?
questions.description: Clarifying whether the user needs full rhythmic reading or primarily pitch recognition scopes the depth of study required.
